Hair Services

Hair Services

Home / Hair Services

A plain-language look at the services you'll commonly find at a salon or salon studio, what they involve, and how to decide what's right for you.

Salon services generally fall into a few broad categories: cutting, coloring, styling, treatments, extensions, and occasion-specific services like bridal hair. Most people book one service at a time, but many of these naturally pair together — a color service is often followed by a cut and blow-dry, for instance, and a treatment might be added onto a coloring appointment to offset the processing. Each guide below breaks down what the service actually involves, what to expect for timing and upkeep, and what's worth asking your stylist before you book.

If you're new to a service, start with the guide itself before booking — it covers the vocabulary you'll need in a consultation, what a fair timeline looks like, and what tends to drive price up or down. That's usually more useful than searching photos alone, since a photo shows the result but not the process, the maintenance commitment, or what your specific hair type might need to do differently to get there.

How to Decide Which Service You Need

If you're not sure where to start, work backward from your goal rather than a specific service name. Want a change in shape without changing color? That's a cutting question. Want a different overall tone or brightness? That's a coloring question, and the specific technique (single-process, highlights, balayage) depends on how much contrast and maintenance you're comfortable with. Want your hair to feel healthier rather than look different? That points toward a treatment rather than a cut or color change. Most consultations start with exactly this kind of goal-first conversation before narrowing down to a specific service.

Combining Services in One Visit

Many appointments combine more than one service — a cut with a color, or a treatment added onto a chemical service to offset processing. When booking, mention every service you're considering upfront rather than adding them once you're already in the chair, since your stylist needs to plan the full appointment length and product order (color typically happens before a cut, for instance) around everything you want done that day.

Booking With Confidence

Whichever service you're after, walking in with a clear sense of what you want — and a realistic idea of timing and cost — tends to produce a better result and a smoother appointment than showing up undecided. Use these guides, plus our Salon Cost Calculator, to prepare before you book.

Services Evolve Too

Techniques and product lines change over the years — what's considered a standard color technique today may look different from what was popular a decade ago. These guides are reviewed periodically to keep terminology and recommendations current, so bookmark this hub and check back rather than relying on older, unrelated sources for the latest terminology.

A Note on Pricing Across Services

Every guide here touches on pricing to some degree, but none can quote exact numbers, since prices vary by professional, region, and current demand. Where a guide discusses cost, treat the framing — what drives price up or down, what's reasonable to ask about — as more useful than any specific dollar figure you might see mentioned elsewhere online.

Start Wherever Makes Sense for You

There's no required order to these guides. If you already know which service you want, jump straight to that page. If you're still deciding, the haircut and hair coloring guides are the two most commonly read first, since most other services build on decisions made in one of those two categories.
